old_man.name: Elder Rowan
old_man.greeting: Welcome back, traveler. The road has been dangerous, but we are alive.

topics.text: Tell me about the camp.
topics.response: We were farmers, merchants, refugees... The Gravekeeper rise drove us here. These tents are all we have left. But you — you fight. That gives us hope.

topics.text: Have you seen anything strange?
topics.response: The graveyard to the east... The dead do not rest easy there. Something ancient keeps them rising. Be careful if you go back.

topics.text: [End Conversation]

cute_girl.name: Lina
cute_girl.greeting: Oh! You fixed up the camp! I am... I am Lina. Thank you for making this place safer.

topics.text: How did you end up here?
topics.response: I was a baker daughter in the city. When the dead started walking, we fled. My family... I do not know if they made it. But I am grateful to be alive.

topics.text: Is there anything I can do to help?
topics.response: If you could clear the graveyard, maybe we could rebuild the city road. People would start coming back. Please... be careful out there.

topics.text: [End Conversation]

blacksmith.name: Garret the Blacksmith
blacksmith.greeting: Hmph. Another traveler. If you need weapons forged, you have come to the right place. I used to make plows and horseshoes. Now it is all swords and shields.

topics.text: Can you forge me something special?
topics.response: I can forge decent blades, but the real materials... they are buried in the graveyard. Bring me rare metal and I will make you something legendary.

topics.text: How did you end up here?
topics.response: I was the finest smith in the valley. When the dead rose, my forge was the first thing they destroyed. I have been tempering steel and tempering my patience ever since.

topics.text: [End Conversation]

tavern_keeper.name: Mira the Tavern Keeper
tavern_keeper.greeting: Welcome, weary soul! Sit down, have a drink. Well... we are out of ale. But I have got stories, and those are free.

topics.text: Any rumors from the road?
topics.response: Travelers say the Gravekeeper was not always a monster. Some say he was a good man once, until something broke inside him. Tragic, really.

topics.text: This place used to be lively, huh?
topics.response: Lively? It was the heart of the village! Singing, dancing, feasts every fortnight. Now it is just me and the rats. But we keep the lights on. Hope is important.

topics.text: [End Conversation]

worried_refugee.name: Anxious Refugee
worried_refugee.greeting: *shivers* Did you hear that last night? Groaning from the graveyard. They are getting closer every day...

topics.text: How are you holding up?
topics.response: The nights are getting colder. My children are sick. I do not know how much longer we can survive here. But at least you fight for us. That means something.

topics.text: Are the zombies really getting closer?
topics.response: Every night I hear them. Scratching at the walls, moaning. Elder Rowan says we are safe, but I have seen them in the treeline. They are watching us.

topics.text: [End Conversation]

weather_watcher.name: Old Sarah
weather_watcher.greeting: Rain is coming. My bones always know. *looks at the sky* Dark clouds gathering over the graveyard...

topics.text: What do you think about the weather?
topics.response: Storm is brewing. Good for the crops — if we had any left. Bad for morale. People get anxious when the sky goes dark. Reminds them of... you know.

topics.text: Tell me about the old days.
topics.response: Oh honey, I remember when this was all green fields. Markets full of flowers, children laughing. Now look at us. Huddled around campfires, jumping at shadows.

topics.text: [End Conversation]

nervous_guard.name: Guard Cedric
nervous_guard.greeting: *grips spear tightly* You... you are heading in there? I was posted here three days ago. I have not slept since. The sounds at night... you would not believe.

topics.text: What have you seen in there?
topics.response: Shadows moving between the tombstones. Things crawling out of fresh graves. And the whispering... always whispering. Like they are calling to someone. Do not go in after dark. Please.

topics.text: Why do you stay if it is so dangerous?
topics.response: Someone has to watch the gate. If I leave, they will pour into the camp while you sleep. I am not brave — I am just too scared to abandon my post. There is a difference.

topics.text: [End Conversation]

grave_digger.name: Old Mortimer
grave_digger.greeting: *taps shovel on ground* Another visitor to the resting place. Do not mind me — just keeping the plots tidy. Though half of them do not stay tidy for long, if you catch my meaning.

topics.text: Do the dead really rise here?
topics.response: Rise? They dance, friend. I have seen bones walk out of coffins, flesh reattach itself. The Gravekeeper did something to this ground. Cursed it. Every grave I dig, I wonder if the occupant will thank me or try to eat me.

topics.text: How long have you been doing this?
topics.response: Forty years I have been digging graves. Started when I was younger than you. Back then it was peaceful work — quiet, respectful. Now? Now I carry a shovel in one hand and a blade in the other. Times change.

topics.text: Any rumors about what is deeper in the graveyard?
topics.response: The crypt. Below the cemetery. I have heard noises from down there — grinding stone, chanting. Something ancient sleeps beneath us. If you are foolish enough to go looking, bring friends. And weapons. Lots of weapons.

topics.text: [End Conversation]

hunter.name: Finn the Hunter
hunter.greeting: *nocks an arrow* Easy now — I almost took you for a wolf. These woods have been restless lately. More beasts than I have seen in twenty years of hunting.

topics.text: What is happening in the forest?
topics.response: The dead are not just in the graveyard anymore. I have seen them in the treeline — shambling through the undergrowth. Something is drawing them here. The forest has always been old, but now it feels... hungry.

topics.text: Are you hunting the undead?
topics.response: I hunt what pays. Wolves, boar, deer — and now these things. They do not bleed like living creatures, but they still fall if you split them open. Silver tip arrows help. Old trick from my grandmother.

topics.text: Can you supply me with anything?
topics.response: I have some spare arrows and dried meat. Not much, but I can trade if you bring me wolf pelts. The wolves are aggressive right now — probably the same magic rot that raised the dead.

topics.text: [End Conversation]

herbalist.name: Briar
herbalist.greeting: *crushes leaves between fingers* Ah, a traveler. You smell of campfire and iron. Come — sit. The forest speaks if you know how to listen.

topics.text: Who are you? What are you doing out here?
topics.response: I am Briar. I was a healer in the city before... everything. Now I live here, among the roots. The forest still grows, even with the dead walking. Life finds a way. Always.

topics.text: Can you make medicine?
topics.response: I can brew remedies for most wounds. The forest has what I need — moonpetal, ghostmoss, shadowbark. Bring me ingredients and I will make you potions that no blacksmith can forge.

topics.text: Do you know anything about the magic raising the dead?
topics.response: *pauses* The forest remembers. Old magic — older than the Gravekeeper. He did not create it. He found it. Buried deep, where even I dare not go. The roots know. The roots fear it.

topics.text: [End Conversation]
